newsitem.title: BELGIUM: COURT SAID TO LOOK INTO NEW DI RUPO CHARGES.
newsitem.headline: COURT SAID TO LOOK INTO NEW DI RUPO CHARGES.

text.p: A commission of Belgian parliamentarians investigating child sex allegations against Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo is set to ask Belgium's highest court to continue its investigation of Di Rupo.
Francophone socialist Di Rupo, a discreet homosexual, has denied any involvement in paedophilia.
"The new allegations must also be investigated by the court, but this time without a deadline," commission member Pierre Chevalier for the opposition VLD told Reuters.

At 2000 GMT the 11-member commission, made up of the main parties, started a final meeting to decide on Di Rupo's fate after hearing the minister himself and Eliane Lieckendael, prosecutor general of the Cour de Cassation earlier on Tuesday.
On Monday the court -- Belgium's only court which can judge ministers and ex-ministers -- told parliament that the original allegations by a sole witness were unfounded.
Members for the opposition parties in the commission said new allegations in a second and third dossier by the Brussels public prosecutor should also be investigated by the court.
"There is no way we could just drop these allegations. It is logical that the court investigates them too," said Didier Reynders for the opposition liberal PRL party.
Commission members for the socialist parties said that the allegations in the second and third report were even flimsier than those in the first report.
"The second file is very different from the first case. It consists of various items of dubious value," PS commission member Serge Moureaux said.
Another socialist member said most of the new allegations had been made anonymously and that the few named testimonies came from mentally ill people.
"The new allegations are too weak. The case against Di Rupo should be dropped," Louis Van Velthoven for the Flemish socialist SP told Reuters.

A continuation of the investigation, unlike the previous investigation withiout a deadline, would leave a sword of Damocles hanging over Di Rupo for weeks, possibly months, and would further paralyse the centre-left government.

Commission members for the Christian Democrat parties shied away from backing either socialist coalition partners or the main, liberal, opposition, but said a compromise between acquittal and indictment should be found.
"It will problably be a long debate," Albert Ghelen of the christan democrat PSC said.

Paul Tant, parliament group leader for the christian democrat CVP, said that parliament should now quickly vote on a new law which would allow the court to investigate any further allegations against Di Rupo or any other ministers without the highly publicised parliamentary commission procedure.
Under current Belgian law only parliament can allow the court to investigate allegations against a minister.

Di Rupo, 45, is one of four deputy prime ministers who each represent a partner in the coalition. As a member of the PS, the second biggest party in the coalition, he is the number two in the government after Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene.
